acceptanceCriteria: A shared example referenced via one unambiguous inclusion site gets a normal ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE verdict; a bare reference to the shared body keeps C-SHARED-EXAMPLE-ONLY.
Two inclusions of the same group are evaluated independently (let overrides / include-call arguments may differ), pinned by a test.
Ambiguous definitions, nested shared groups, include calls inside examples/hooks, non-literal names and loop-generated examples refuse with distinct named codes.

Receipt join: an RSpec receipt row whose id/full_description identifies the inclusion maps to the qualified reference, or abstains; requirements in test-source-analysis-v0.md; focused tests; dogfood CEM; Closes #1164.
body: GitHub #1164. Every example inside shared_examples/shared_examples_for is INELIGIBLE with C-SHARED-EXAMPLE-ONLY; there is no way to evaluate it at a specific inclusion site, though RSpec ids ([1:3:2:1]), JUnit file and full_description ("behaves like NAME") identify the inclusion. Proposal: accept an inclusion-qualified reference (spec/x_spec.rb:<include_line>>spec/support/y.rb:<example_line>, or same:<line>), resolve the include call and its unique definition, run existing hygiene with subject/described_class/lets and pending/skip from the including context, and return ELIGIBLE/INELIGIBLE per inclusion.
title: GH #1164: test-validity (Ruby): inclusion-qualified evaluation of shared_examples instead of always C-SHARED-EXAMPLE-ONLY
